content: This medication is prescribed solely for your current medical condition. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and proceed with your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to make up for the missed one. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not freeze this product, as freezing reduces the amount of atovaquone your body can absorb, potentially diminishing its effectiveness. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in August 2024. It is important to note that this document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Before taking atovaquone, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications may decrease the level of atovaquone in your body, potentially affecting its efficacy. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away.
